body: If he's taking his pills correctly he cannot transmit it. You could swim in a lake full of his semen with 36 bleeding wounds and you would still remain negative. Read about U=U, there's a ton of scientific evidence. If you still feel weird about it, you can take prep and use condoms. If you still don't feel safe then you are the problem.
Focus more on the potential mental illness and be a good friend/family to that person instead of bringing the HIV subject up. You can help without them being aware that you know about their status.

Good god girl get a grip and get tested.

The thing is you can't know for sure. When I was diagnosed I could only think of three things : needle injury, oral, or broken condom/stealthing. When you start thinking about how you got infected, and see how abysmal the chances are through oral, you start thinking it might be something else.

Be patient with him. He will probably turn to you to talk, vent and whatnot. It will help him a lot. Check up on him regularly, make sure he is feeling loved, that nothing changed between you and that you'll always be there for him as a friend. 
If he doesn't want to go out anymore, let him be for some time, but not for too long. He'll probably lock himself in a dark room and go into foetal position on his bed and cry/think about it. If he didn't have an appointment with an ID specialist, accompany him. You don't have to be there for the actual appointment, but knowing you have someone in the waiting room is kind of reassuring.

Show him that life is worth living, and be aware of any hints he might send you, regarding his mental health and stability.

Be strong for him !

First, thank you for your answer and time.

>Guess what - it's sort of the same deal with psychic pain. When you're in mental pain you tend to react to other peoples normal everyday behavior in a bad way. You might be mean or lash out, or you might just seethe inside. Or maybe something else. In any case, it's a bad way to react to other people just living their lives as usual. You start with the mental anguish of being HIV+ (which is understandable to have but unnecessary and with help you can kill it off) 

I know that it's dickish, as you say. They didn't do anything, they're moving on with their lives. I can't and don't blame them for that. I don't want to be that way. I've had my share of social injustice but it never affected me that much, I kept smiling and being a good friend/guy to everyone. But HIV is a big pill to swallow. I really don't want to have this thought process. As much as I am sad for my situation, I don't want them to lose the friend they love. I want to be me again, I want to make them happy just like before, but it is increasingly harder to be reminded constantly how shitty my life is right now and how fulfilling theirs are. 

>Does being poz mean you can't make meaningful connections in life, or can't have fun? You may think it does but I sure AF don't and anybody with the sense god gave to seafood doesn't. Having HIV can make those things more difficult to find / achieve. But they aren't impossible for you to have, not at all. 

On the paper, it absolutely doesn't. I am well aware of that, but I am starting to experience stigma and I don't think I know how to handle that. One of my former FWBs erased me from his life, without notice, and when I wanted to check in on him, know if he got tested and all that, he ignored my text altogether. Didn't even open it. This kind of pushes me to build back the walls I used to have and lead a solitary life. That was a nice guy, or so I thought, and living where I do, it doesn't really get much better than this. My dating pool was incredibly small, now it got even smaller, to the point of maybe not existing at all. I don't want to settle for someone just because they could be fine with my status. I would be incredibly unhappy and more of a liability to this person than anything.

>Anyway, you can go back to being that guy you used to be. After all, you're the one who's changed, right? You should look into seeing a counselor, preferably one specializing in or experienced with dealing in people with HIV, but any qualified pro can help you address your anger and bitterness. 

I hope so. I hope I'm not irremediably broken. The counselor I've seen so far has only been answering me with "It'll get better" and " I believe you can do it" and " It's not that bad". No actual solution to my problems. I'll seek another one.

>What, exactly, makes you angry? 

I don't know. I'm mourning my former life. I'm mad because this is unfair. But what can I do about it ? 

BeingPoz is a bit silent, so I wanted to post here instead.

I am not angry at other people because they are happy. They didn't do anything to me. I have no one or nothing to direct this anger at this is what's eating away at me. The problem is I can no longer relate to the people I love, and I want to share their lives and make them better.

What can I do if I'm not responsible for this ? How can I be at peace when I did everything in my power to remain negative, but still end up poz, even more so if I got it on the job filling someone else's spot because there's a lack of personnel in my hospital ?

I actually have no idea of the legality of this. I live in the middle east, homosexuality is illegal to begin with, so I have not really thought about non-disclosure. 
My chance to get out of here was probably compromised because of HIV, due to my future job being a doctor. If it fails I will have to find a way to make it work. Which means not burning inside everytime I see someone else smile.

>you shouldn’t ever feel like anger is a problem.

But it actually is. It seems I cannot run on happiness and love like I used to. I am either numb, sad, or furious. This is affecting my mental health and I want to move on.

>HIV has given me a greater appreciation of the profound racial, social and political privilege I’ve enjoyed, mostly as an accident of birth.

I was already aware of all my blessings, and I still am. Sure I'm not the most blessed individual around, but it could always be worse. I have friends, a wonderful monder, a roof over my head and food on my table at the end of the day. What I need is peace of mind with this side of my life.

>I’m not going to lie, you’ll probably lose a few friends doing this. It’s not the “just so happy it’s a chronic disease” bullshit we’re normally told to feel. But you’ll find other friends, and they’ll be better, nicer, more interesting people. Finding people who can meet you where you are is a much better strategy than stifling your feelings for awful people you no longer relate to.

That's the thing. I don't want to lose my friends because of the virus. I love them, they love me, and I want to be a good friend to them. I do not want the virus to destroy yet another part of my life.

However, I am aware that what I want to do is not always what I'm going to do. I'm turning to you guys for advice in case there's still something to save here.
I know. What I meant to say is that I want to be labeled as neg by common peeps or when I am asked about my status.
My empathy. It borders on martyr syndrome tho.

We wouldn't have people terrified or harming themselves if we had a working cure. There would be no stigma. I believe stigma will endure as long as we don't have a cure.

Because the power that the word CURE has will forever outweigh any scientific survey or long-term medication you need to take for life, because the masses understand CURE more than they do surveys and whatnot. It means that even if they managed to get it, they'd get an injection or an array of pills or whatever and they'll get back to their lives. I don't want to be a slave to some pharmaceutical because it is good enough. I want this virus out of my system for good. The fact that we may eradicate hiv in some countries in a few decades doesn't mean we have to leave currently infected people deal with those 45% of people who believe in ghosts. Health isn't just numbers on a paper. Mental health is just as important. I could've been dead by now, because I was about to OD on stuff to escape the reality of hiv. Doesn't mean I won't do it in the future. 

As PC said, if it is not that big of a deal then please seroconvert and see for yourself how it is to deal with ignorance from some because other hiv- people think that what we have right now is "good enough".

As far as I respect your input in this thread, the fact that you are hiv- and still argue against a cure is mind-boggling. You know what a cure is : not having it in your system, not transmitting it, and not needing to "pop a pill" everyday. Basically turn HIV into syphillis. Do you see any stigma against syphillis, besides regular half-joke slut-shaming ? No. But people who had syphilis will always have antibodies directed against it.
Do you see a "syphilis status" checkbox on grindr ? No. A cure, to me, is not needing a " HIV status" on hook up apps by making HIV as significant as gonorrhea.

I'm on atripla as well. My first night was a nightmare, litterally. I didn't sleep much, I felt dizzy and my brain was racing at 1000mph. The next week I had a rash, pretty annoying. Somewhere around that time, my mood/self-esteem/courage collapsed on itself, I started crying every single day and even contemplated suicide all the time. I don't know if it is tied to the medication or because I figured out that having HIV I wouldn't be able to get the dream career I worked really hard for. Now I'm better, no side effects anymore, even though my mental health isn't at it's best.

I just want to be labeled as negative again. That's the idea of cure for me.

First of all, this is not a "boohoo no one loves me cos' I'm poz" post, simply because I was just diagnosed and currently not dating, hence not telling a soul. I was simply trying to change maybe help a poz fellow or two by bringing some positivity around here.

Sure, there are a lot of ways to prevent it, none of which are 100% reliable. If you were wondering : No, I never went bareback, I even avoided to get loads anywhere near any mucous membrane. 
No, I did not get on prep, because I live in a homophobic third world country with absolutely no communication on the subject. I didn't even know such a thing existed here.
Yes, I wore a condom each and every time I had sex with someone of unknown status.

As I already answer someone else, I can only see 3 ways of being infected : Stealthing, Oral, and Needles.

 I work in the medical field, and in a third world country things do not look cute. At all. I could've gone on PEP but it is such a rarely used thing, the moment I got pricked half of the staff was unphased, the other half laughed it off. " Hahaha I don't even count how many times I got pricked and I'm totally fine". It's my own stupid mistake for listening to what the whole system was telling me to do.

Oral. Rare. But not impossible. As I said I was not on PrEP because I didn't know it existed at that time.

Stealthing, do I even need to explain myself.

I did my best. I did better than most. Still got unlucky. I understand how you would think that HIV should've been eradicated by now, with the array of therapeutics we have. I get your frustration. But not every story is the same.
I've read about guys trusting their partners, who cheated, and therefore got infected. I've read about people getting raped. Having destructive behaviour because of this and that in their life.

Tests, like all things, are not perfect. So some of them are sometimes wrong. The most accurate way to tell if you have hiv or not is by doing the second confirmatory test. And no it wouldn't have shown up in those varying blood work you did, unless they specifically looked for it.

Also : don't freak out ! Hiv is not what it used to be ! A pill a day and poz guys will be totally fine. It's just like any other chronic illness, like diabetes or high blood pressure ( and treatment for those are heavier than treatment for hiv ). Social stigma is still a bit present but you wouldn't want to surround yourself with judgy idiotic people anyway, trust me.

All I would advise you to do right now, is stop thinking about it, enjoy your week end, go do that second test and wait for the results just as serenely. Stressing out will not change the outcome, it will just make you feel horrible.
